extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department administrators, job applicants, conference organizers, and AMS Notices contributors/readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards from the AMS Notices covering professional hiring-practice recommendations, the AMS academic-employment cover sheet, undergraduate prize submission rules, and policies for meeting/conference announcements and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and accurate applicant response
rubrics_metrics.description: The ]CEO believes that every applicant is entitled to the courtesy of a prompt and accurate response that provides timely information about his/her status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, after receiving an application institutions should (1) acknowledge receipt of the application immediately; and (2) provide information as to the current status of the application, as soon as possible. The ]CEO recommends a triage-based response informing the applicant that he/she (a) is not being considered further; (b) is not among the top candidates; or (c) is a strong match for the position.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS Standard Cover Sheet: include and complete
rubrics_metrics.description: This cover sheet is provided as an aid to departments in processing job applications. It should be included with your application material. Please print or type. Do not send this form to the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required/expected fields and instructions: Last Name, First Name, Middle Names, Social Security Number (optional), Address (through June 1996), Home Phone, e-mail Address, Current Institutional Affiliation, Work Phone, Highest Degree and Source, Ph.D. Advisor, expected Ph.D. date if not yet held. Indicate mathematical subject area(s) using the 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification (list primary interest first; secondary interests optional). Give a brief synopsis of current research interests (avoid special mathematical symbols and do not write outside the boxed area). State most recent post-Ph.D. position (university/company, title, dates). Indicate the position being applied for and posting code if applicable. Indicate whether you wish to be considered for temporary positions (Yes/No) and check appropriate boxes (Postdoctoral, 2+ Year, 1 Year). List names, affiliations, and e-mail addresses of up to four individuals who will provide letters of recommendation; mark box for each individual already asked to send a letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate research prize: eligibility and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is awarded each year to an undergraduate student (or students having submitted joint work) for outstanding research in mathematics. Any student who is an undergraduate in a college or university in the United States or its possessions, or Canada or Mexico, is eligible to be considered for this prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research need not be confined to a single paper; it may be contained in several papers. However, the paper(s) to be considered must be submitted while the student is an undergraduate; they cannot be submitted after graduation. The research paper(s) may be submitted by the student or a nominator. All submissions for the prize must include at least one letter of support from a person (usually a faculty member) familiar with the student's research. Publication of research is not required. Recipients are selected by a standing joint committee of the AMS, MAA, and SIAM; the committee's decisions are final. (Example deadline given: papers submitted for consideration no later than June 30, 1996, by students who were undergraduates in December 1995.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices Meetings & Conferences: publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An announcement will be published in the Notices if it contains a call for papers and specifies the place, date, subject (when applicable), and the speakers; a second announcement will be published only if there are changes or necessary additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an announcement has appeared, the event will be briefly noted in every third issue until it has been held and a reference will be given to the month, year, and page of the issue in which the complete information appeared. Asterisks (*) mark those announcements containing new or revised information. In general, announcements of meetings and conferences held in North America carry only the date, title of meeting, place of meeting, names of speakers (or a general statement on the program), deadlines for abstracts or contributed papers, and source of further information. Meetings held outside North America may carry more detailed information. If there is any application deadline with respect to participation in the meeting, this fact should be noted. All communications on meetings and conferences in the mathematical sciences should be sent to the Editor of the Notices in care of the American Mathematical Society in Providence or electronically to notices@math.ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and repetition policy for meeting listings
rubrics_metrics.description: To allow participants to arrange travel plans, organizers of meetings are urged to submit information early enough to allow the listing to appear in more than one issue of the Notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings should be received in Providence six months prior to the scheduled date of the meeting to appear in more than one issue. The complete listing of the Mathematics Calendar is published only in the September issue. The March, June, and December issues include, along with new announcements, references to any previously announced meetings and conferences occurring within the twelve-month period following the month of those issues. New information about meetings and conferences that will occur later than the twelve-month period will be announced once in full and will not be repeated until the date of the conference falls within the twelve-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/workshop submission formats and selection procedures (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many workshop and conference announcements specify required submission formats, abstract lengths, deadlines, and the intended structure of proceedings/selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from notices: 'Paper submissions, in the form of four-page extended abstracts, are solicited ... sent before January 15, 1996, to co-chairs; Workshop proceedings will be published in book form; Selected papers will appear in [a journal].' 'Extended abstracts (one to three pages) for contributed talks should be sent before March 8; the program committee will make a selection before April 1; invited speakers will be invited to submit full papers, which will undergo usual refereeing; poster sessions or software demonstration proposals (one page) may be organized.' 'Prospective contributors should submit an extended abstract of approximately two pages by Feb 15.' These specify concrete expectations for abstract length, submission deadlines, possible poster or demo sessions, and that accepted papers may be refereed for publication in proceedings or journals.
